current_bottleneck: 289e showed that the history-memory world-model backbone now preserves shared structure and active mean reversion, but the deterministic smooth-regression target still oversmooths the local move-size law. The next bottleneck is the next-step output formulation, not just the recurrent state architecture.
last_result_summary: Iteration 123 ran 289e-v0 and tied the world-model local frontier at 3/11. It materially improved corr_ratio to 0.952 and active MR pass rate to 83.3%, but change KS remained 0/25 and jump q90/q99 regressed to 0.071/0.111. The current world-model backbone is therefore treated as structurally viable, with the remaining blocker shifting to deterministic output formulation.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 290a-v0: keep the 289e history-memory world-model backbone, but replace smooth next-change regression with a discretized normalized-change output target driven by the same hidden state.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
